disk_footprint.note: What a database occupies after 200 documents, per store profile and collection count. Blocks, heads, indexes and the log, everything the directory holds.

document_ops.note: Documents created and read back one at a time, 200 of each, through the same mutator and fetcher every platform uses. Measured with a wall clock natively and with `performance.now()` in the browser, so the two are the same operation counted the same way.

memory.note: Peak resident set size of a process that ran one workload and nothing else. Each row is its own child process, because peak RSS only ever rises and cases sharing a process would all report the largest of them. baseline is the process floor, to be subtracted from the rest; open is an empty database opened and closed; seed writes 1000 documents; scan writes them and reads every one back.
memory.title: Resident memory

browser_storage.note: The regolith key/value path in a browser tab: 200 operations of a 256 byte value. `batched write` puts every write in one transaction; `write per commit` opens and commits one per write, and the gap between them is what batching buys.

groups.name: per operation
groups.note: Allocations observed across the whole process while performing the operation, divided by how many were performed. A ceiling on the operation's own cost, not an attribution of it.

groups.name: collection load bytes
groups.note: Bytes allocated across the whole process per collection a transaction loads into its catalog, with that many collections loaded into the one transaction.

allocs.note: How many allocations each path makes, averaged over 200 operations. Deterministic: a count does not move because the runner was busy, so this is comparable across every run whatever the load guard said.
allocs.title: Allocations per operation

artifact_size.note: What each shipped artifact weighs. The browser bundle is also reported compressed, because that is what a browser downloads.

write_baseline_counters_indexes.note: On-disk Immediate durability; 256 requests per writer; 3 fresh-store repetitions. HTTP execution without sockets, signing or ACP. Latencies include client-conflict and engine-exhausted requests. Storage conflicts exclude pre-commit query conflicts; client conflicts count requests returned with a transaction conflict. Engine retries count replay executions after a losing attempt; exhaustion is reported separately. Retired retry layers report zero by definition.
